findings.title: traceID no longer attached to "Plugin Request Completed" log line
findings.body: The old logRequest explicitly fetched the trace ID and appended it to the log params: `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false); if traceID != "" { logParams = append(logParams, "traceID", traceID) }`. That code has been deleted in this PR and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext (pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go) only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname — it never reads or forwards the trace ID via log.WithContextualAttributes. Nothing in the modified LoggerMiddleware recovers it either, so every "Plugin Request Completed" log line now loses its trace correlation. Unless pkg/infra/log's FromContext implementation silently injects a traceID (which the old explicit code suggests it does not), this is an observability regression: distributed tracing can no longer be joined back to the request completion log line.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
findings.body: A brand-new client middleware was added that mutates the request context with endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname via log.WithContextualAttributes on every QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics path. No contextual_logger_middleware_test.go was added, and the sibling metrics_middleware_test.go does not exercise this middleware. There is consequently no regression protection for: (a) the order in which contextual attributes are appended (the existing pCtx.DataSourceInstanceSettings / pCtx.User nil checks), (b) the assumption that downstream LoggerMiddleware actually picks the attributes up via FromContext, or (c) the still-missing traceID described in the related finding. A test should assert the expected key/value pairs on the context after each entrypoint, mirroring what the deleted instrumentContext tests would have caught.

findings.title: Test function still named after the old middleware
findings.body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the helper references were updated (e.g. newMetricsMiddleware on line 78), but the top-level test func TestInstrumentationMiddleware was left unchanged. After this rename the test name no longer matches the production type it exercises; CI tooling, `--run` filtering and any coverage reports will keep advertising the obsolete name. Rename it to TestMetricsMiddleware for consistency with the rest of the rename.
